method: Independent formulas applied to original prediction and reference CSV/text; no inference or evaluator function imported.
assessment: Share with caveats; code, numerical reconciliation and corrected UTC integer export independently verified.

code_review.finding: Cache identity includes rgb_aggregation, video path/size/mtime, max_seconds and all three frontend source hashes; cache content hash and frame count are checked.
Both prespecified modes run on every retained video. gap15 reuses that video's gap10 trace. All 12 command lines omit references; all source summaries match frozen hashes.

floor(gap_s*fps+1e-9) is a missing-sample-count limit; it counts missing samples divided by FPS, not elapsed distance between surrounding observed samples. At the selected frame rates the tolerance has no material effect.
Tests and sources frozen before video inference, all candidates retained. These are development/regression videos, not held-out validation.

At UBFC and Kaggle FPS, gap10 is reduced from 3 missing frames to 2 relative to V21 rounding. Both videos have no missing merged or ROI samples. The other four videos have unchanged gap10 frame limits; six-video frontend validity and geometry match.
Actual Python/OpenCV/MediaPipe/numpy/pandas/scipy/matplotlib versions were recorded during this run; supplemental record does not itself demonstrate cross-environment reproducibility.

required_caveats: data1 uses the frozen mtime-minus-duration start estimate, not verified hardware synchronization. No delay was fitted or selected from HR errors. Polar HR notifications are the user-designated reference, not ECG.
MAE/RMSE/P5 condition on accepted/reference-eligible windows; R5 uses all reference-eligible planned windows. Common comparisons retain the intersection of all six local/DP branches.
Output rate and waveform availability are not accuracy. Removing two data1 outputs changes own-window composition; therefore both own and common results must be retained.
UBFC SNR increases while HR MAE/RMSE worsen slightly. Reference-band power concentration does not guarantee the selected peak is more accurate or establish waveform morphology.
Overlap-window errors are dependent; descriptive LoA is not an independent-subject confidence interval. All processing remains offline.
The real-video results do not validate the hypothesis that median quantization caused the data1 shared wrong-frequency peak.
